audience: A lay reader who has just read about five common defenses.
shows: Five defenses as five walls between an agent and the internet, each with a named gap. One path passes through every gap.
complements: The text argues each defense in turn with evidence; the figure holds all five in one view so the reader sees the same shape repeat.
surrounding_text: Hiding the passwords: a password was never what the agent needed to read; it reads the inbox. Putting the agent in a box: it writes something that a trusted program outside the box will run. Allowing only approved destinations: an approved destination can record what is sent to it. Having a second AI watch the first: the watcher is a model too. Asking you first: the person asked is a tired person.
alt: An agent, shown inverted, below your private data and above the internet, with five walls in between and a dashed path through a gap in each. Passwords hidden, but the inbox is read. Boxed in, but it writes things others run. Approved list, but the list has a recorder on it. Watched, by a model. Asked, by a person. It shows that each defense leaves a way through.
caption: Five walls, and the gap each one leaves.
